newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan big brokers to unveil 96/97 results in April.
newsitem.headline: Japan big brokers to unveil 96/97 results in April.

text.p: Japan's top four securities houses said on Wednesday that they will announce their earnings results for the 1996/97 business year ending March 31 in late April, about two weeks earlier than in the past.
The four are Nomura Securities Co Ltd, Daiwa Securities Co Ltd, Nikko Securities Co Ltd and Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.
Nomura is scheduled to announce both parent and group earnings results for 1996/97 on April 24, and Nikko on April 25, spokesmen at the companies said.

Daiwa is scheduled to announce parent results on April 25 and group results on May 6, while Yamaichi will announce parent earnings on April 28 and group results on May 7, spokesmen at the two firms also said.
Industry sources said that the big securities houses, which traditionally announce their parent earnings results on the same day in mid-May, decided to disclose the figures as early as possible.

Yamaichi and Nikko are expected to stop reporting earnings forecasts for the coming business year and start announcing quarterly earnings results from the current business year after Nomura and Daiwa took such measures in the past, they said.

Last month, Yamaichi revised its parent current profit forecast for 1996/97 to nil from the previous projection of 19.00 million yen against actual 15.13 million yen in profit in 1995/96. It sees its parent net loss for 1996/97 at 163.0 billion yen against earlier expected net loss of 110.00 billion yen and actual net profit of 15.90 million yen in 1995/96.
Yamaichi and three other big brokers have said that they would provide financial aid to their financial affiliates in 1996/97, which would result in net losses.

Last December Nikko revised its earnings forecast for 1996/97 downward to a parent current profit of 40 billion yen from a previous forecast of 60 billion yen and actual 65 billion yen in the profit in 1995/96. It also expected a parent net loss of 95 billion yen compared with the previous forecast of a net profit of 24 billion yen and an actual net profit of 33.76 billion yen in 1995/96.

Financial sources said that Daiwa's parent net loss was expected at about 80 billion yen in 1996/97 against an actual parent net profit of 43.69 billion yen in 1995/96. Daiwa is also expected to post a parent current profit of about 60 billion yen against an actual profit of 62.56 billion yen in the previous year.

Nomura's parent current profit is expected at about 100 billion yen and its parent net loss of 300 billion yen against actual 91.49 billion yen in parent current profit in 1995/96 and 23.1 billion yen in net profit.
